problem_statement: AgentStudio's current specialist execution pipeline lacks quality validation, cost optimization, resilience, and observability. Specialists succeed by exiting with code 0 regardless of output quality, all use the same model regardless of complexity, there is no iterative retry-and-fix loop, no abandonment detection, no file-based artifact chain for workflow resumability, no human checkpoints during execution, no progressive skill loading, no scope enforcement, no declarative hooks, and no diagnostic escalation when all retries fail.
solution_overview: Implement a 10-phase upgrade plan that adds: (1) complexity scoring with model routing to optimize cost, (2) iterative task loops with quality gates for reliability, (3) anti-abandonment detection for persistence, (4) file-based agent communication for auditability and resumability, (5) cost tracking dashboard for visibility, (6) human checkpoint UI for control, (7) progressive skill loading for efficiency, (8) scope enforcement for safety, (9) declarative hooks for extensibility, and (10) deep agent personas with bug council for advanced diagnostics.

needs: Reliable agent execution with quality guarantees
Control over execution flow with approval gates
Audit trail of agent decisions and outputs

must_have.name: Database Migration System
must_have.description: Lightweight schema versioning with up/down migrations to safely evolve the SQLite schema across upgrade phases
acceptance_criteria: Migration runner executes pending migrations on app startup
Each migration has a version number and up/down SQL
Current schema version is tracked in the database
Failed migrations roll back cleanly

must_have.name: Complexity Scoring & Model Routing
must_have.description: Score every task by complexity (0-14) and route to the cheapest capable model (haiku/sonnet/opus). Saves 40-60% on API costs.
acceptance_criteria: Every specialist task gets a complexity score before execution
Specialists spawn with the correct --model flag based on score
Users can set workspace-level cost preference (economy/balanced/power)
agent_sessions table records model used and complexity score
Simple tasks consistently route to haiku, complex to opus

must_have.name: Task Loop with Quality Gates
must_have.description: Wrap every specialist execution in an iterative loop: Execute -> Validate -> Pass? Done. Fail? Fix -> Escalate model -> Retry.
acceptance_criteria: Quality gates (tsc, eslint, npm test, build) run after each specialist completes
Failed gates trigger retry with fix context appended to prompt
Model escalates after 2 consecutive failures (haiku->sonnet->opus)
Stuck loop detection triggers immediate escalation
Max 10 iterations before surfacing to user
UI shows iteration count, model tier, and gate results

must_have.name: Anti-Abandonment Detection
must_have.description: Detect when a specialist gives up and inject a re-engagement prompt instead of accepting the failure.
acceptance_criteria: Specialist output analyzed for abandonment patterns before marking complete
Detected abandonment triggers re-engagement prompt
Re-engagement varies by category (direct, premature, deflection)
Legitimate completion phrases are whitelisted
Integrates with task loop - abandonment counts toward escalation

must_have.name: File-Based Agent Communication Chain
must_have.description: Specialists write structured output to shared task directories. Subsequent specialists read prior outputs. Makes workflows auditable, resumable, and debuggable.
acceptance_criteria: Each task plan creates a .agentstudio/{conversation-id}/ directory
Each specialist output is saved as structured markdown
Downstream specialists receive prior task outputs as context
State file tracks progress and enables resumption
User can close app and resume multi-task workflows

must_have.name: Cost Tracking Dashboard
must_have.description: Track token usage and estimated cost per model, per agent, per conversation. Show savings from model routing.
acceptance_criteria: Cost calculated using current Anthropic pricing per model
Conversation-level cost breakdown available in UI
Workspace-level cost dashboard shows spend by model and agent
Savings vs all-Opus metric displayed
Optional budget alerts at 80% and 100% thresholds

must_have.name: Human Checkpoint UI
must_have.description: Explicit approval gates before critical actions: merging worktrees, executing multi-task plans, completing phases.
acceptance_criteria: Phase transitions require user approval
Worktree merges require user approval
Checkpoint modal shows what/why/risk details
Execution pauses until checkpoint is resolved
Rejected checkpoints allow user feedback

nice_to_have.name: Progressive Skill Loading
nice_to_have.description: Load skills in tiers: metadata always, instructions on activation, code examples on demand. Reduces token usage.
acceptance_criteria: Skills parsed into 3 tiers on import
Keyword matching first (no LLM call for obvious matches)
Specialist prompts receive Tier 2 by default, Tier 3 on demand
Token usage reduction is measurable

nice_to_have.name: Scope Enforcement Layer
nice_to_have.description: Prevent specialists from modifying files outside their assigned task scope.
acceptance_criteria: Each decomposed task has scope constraints
Post-execution validation checks changed files against scope
Scope violations treated as gate failures in task loop
Violating file changes reverted before retry

nice_to_have.name: Declarative Hooks System
nice_to_have.description: User-defined automation hooks in YAML that trigger on agent events.
acceptance_criteria: Users define hooks in .agentstudio/hooks.yaml
Hooks fire on correct events (15+ event types)
Blocking hooks pause execution
Default hooks auto-generated per project type

nice_to_have.name: Deep Agent Personas & Bug Council
nice_to_have.description: Enriched specialist personas with war stories and red flags. Bug Council of 5 diagnostic agents activates on persistent failures.
acceptance_criteria: Default specialists have enriched personas
Bug Council activates after 3 opus failures
5 diagnostic agents run in parallel
Perspectives synthesized into actionable solution
Solution fed back for one more attempt

performance: Quality gate execution completes within 2 minutes per specialist task
Complexity scoring adds < 1 second overhead per task
Cost calculation is synchronous (no API calls needed)
reliability: Task loop prevents silent failures from reaching the user
Anti-abandonment detection catches 95%+ of give-up phrases
File-based artifacts survive app crashes and restarts
security: Scope enforcement prevents specialists from modifying forbidden files
Hook commands are sandboxed with configurable timeouts
No raw shell execution without user-defined hook config

constraints.compatibility: Must not break existing generalist/orchestrator/specialist flow
constraints.database: All schema changes via migration system (Sprint 0 prerequisite)

success_metrics: 40-60% cost reduction from model routing (measured via cost dashboard)
95%+ specialist tasks pass quality gates before completing
0% silent failures (all failures surface to user or trigger escalation)
Workflow resumability across app restarts for in-progress plans
< 3 second overhead per task from all new middleware layers
